sources.note: Nothing for Lunana. Sec. 9.7.2 p.555: the three yakherd varieties of Dzongkha (Laya, Lingzhi, Lungnagnak/Lunana) 'have so far not been studied'; p.558 lists Lunana as a pastoralists' variety of Dzongkha located in Garsa (Gasa) county. The book's stress section (7.3.3 pp.241-243) does not mention Lunana or Dzongkha varieties.

sources.citation: Tshering, Karma & George van Driem. 2019. The Grammar of Dzongkha, revised and expanded. Himalayan Linguistics Archive 7.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Lunana. Printed p.4: 'Peculiar dialects of Dzongkha are spoken in the far north, viz. the dialect of the alpine yakherd communities of Lingzhi, Laya and Lunana in the northwest Bhutan. Much of the couleur locale of these northern dialects results from structural and lexical similarities with Tibetan.' The phonology described is explicitly that of the standard Wang/Thê dialect only.
